Vest, told 1999 graduates, "being unencumbered by the thought process” leads to greater happiness. Photo by Donna Coveney. In 1968, during a tumultuous period in US political and racial history, Black students at MIT formed the MIT Black Students’ Union (BSU). The BSU was created with two goals in mind: to support each other and to bring more Black students to the Institute. At that time, Black students made up less than 1% of each 1,000-member undergraduate class.
